Why go: time with elephants without riding or shows

Many of Thailand's elephants spent their working lives in logging and later carrying tourists. This sanctuary in the hills above Bophut runs visits without riding, bathing or shows. You start with a short introduction to the animals' backgrounds, prepare fruit and vegetables, feed them, and then walk with them and watch them in their area. The 3 hour visit adds a longer walk and a vegetarian meal.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: families with young children, as the 1.5 hour visit fits between nap times and the transfer is short.
  • Good for: anyone who wants to see elephants without supporting riding.
  • Choose something else if you want a strictly observation-only experience: this sanctuary lets guests touch the elephants. Compare the options in our elephant sanctuary guide.
  • Combining with sightseeing? The 4x4 safari with elephant feeding adds temples and a waterfall.

Good to know

  • Safety: elephants are large and can move suddenly. Stay where the keepers place you, keep your hands flat when feeding and never stand behind an elephant.
  • Clothing: the sanctuary asks for modest clothes and closed shoes. The ground is muddy after rain.
  • Timing: morning visits are cooler and, in the rainy season, usually drier.
  • Ethics check: a good sanctuary limits visitor numbers and does not let elephants perform. If you see anything that worries you, tell us; partner feedback shapes what we sell.

Which visit to book

Families with children under 6 usually find the 1.5 hour visit long enough: feeding is the highlight and small children lose interest during the walk. The 3 hour visits give more time to watch the elephants behave naturally, which is the part most adults remember. In the hot season (March to May) the morning slot is noticeably cooler, and in the rainy season it is usually drier. Plan a swim or a quiet afternoon afterwards; you will be muddy.
